q.t: Is 14 even or odd?
q.e: 14 things can be put into 7 pairs with none left over, so 14 is even.

q.t: Is 27 even or odd?
q.e: Pairing 27 things leaves 1 left over, so 27 is odd.

q.t: Gundappa has 4 rows of coconut trees with 5 trees in each row. How many trees are there?
q.e: 4 equal rows of 5: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20.

q.t: How much money is 3 notes of ₹10 and 2 coins of ₹5 (in ₹)?
q.e: ₹30 from the notes and ₹10 from the coins.

q.t: Which of these numbers is even?
q.e: A number is even when its ones digit is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8 — 36 ends in 6.

q.t: The number just after an odd number is always:
q.e: Odd means one left over without a partner; adding 1 gives that one a partner, so the next number is even.

q.t: There are 6 coconut trees and 5 coconuts are plucked from each. How many coconuts in all?
How many even numbers are there from 1 to 10?
q.k: len([x for x in range(1,11) if x%2==0])
q.e: They are 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 — every second number.

q.t: How many pairs can you make from 12 socks?
q.e: Each pair uses 2 socks, and 12 is 6 twos.

q.t: A number has 8 in its ones place. The number is:
q.e: Only the ones digit decides even or odd, because tens, hundreds and so on always pair up fully.

q.t: Which of these numbers is odd?
q.e: 415 ends in 5, an odd digit, so one is left over after pairing.

q.t: How many even numbers are there between 20 and 30 (not counting 20 and 30)?
q.k: len([x for x in range(21,30) if x%2==0])
q.e: They are 22, 24, 26 and 28.

q.t: There are 3 trays. Each tray has 4 rows of 3 laddoos. How many laddoos in all?
q.e: One tray has 4 × 3 = 12 laddoos, and 3 trays have 12 + 12 + 12 = 36.

q.t: How much is 2 notes of ₹50, 3 notes of ₹10 and 4 coins of ₹2 (in ₹)?
Using the digits 1 and 6 once each, which 2-digit number is even?
q.e: 16 ends in 6 (even); 61 ends in 1 (odd).

q.t: How many odd numbers are there from 1 to 100?
q.k: len([x for x in range(1,101) if x%2])
q.e: Numbers go odd, even, odd, even…, so half of the 100 numbers are odd.

q.t: 23 children try to stand in pairs. How many children are left without a partner?
q.e: 23 is odd: 11 pairs use 22 children and 1 is left over.

q.t: Coins placed in 2 equal rows always make:
q.e: Two equal rows means every coin in one row has a partner in the other — that is what even means.

q.t: How much is 5 notes of ₹20 and 5 coins of ₹5 (in ₹)?
q.e: ₹100 from the notes and ₹25 from the coins.

q.t: The ones digit of an even number can be:
q.e: Tens and hundreds always pair up, so only the ones digit decides — and 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 pair up.
Each odd number has one left over; the two left-overs pair with each other, so the total is even (16).
12 pairs up fully and 5 has one left over, so the total still has one left over (17).

q.t: You add any three odd numbers. The answer is always:
q.e: Two of the left-over ones pair up, but the third is left alone — so the total is odd.

q.t: From 1 to 100, are there more even numbers or more odd numbers?
q.e: Odd and even take turns: 1 odd, 2 even, 3 odd … 100 even, so they split 50 and 50.

q.t: Write the 10 numbers from 20 to 29. How many of them are odd?
q.k: len([x for x in range(20,30) if x%2])
q.e: Ten numbers in a row take turns even, odd, even, odd…, so 5 are odd: 21, 23, 25, 27, 29.

q.t: A shop has 4 shelves. Each shelf has 6 rows with 5 cups in each row. How many cups in all?
q.e: One shelf has 6 × 5 = 30 cups, and 4 shelves have 30 + 30 + 30 + 30 = 120.

q.t: What is the smallest 3-digit odd number?
q.e: The smallest 3-digit number is 100, which is even, so the next one, 101, is the smallest odd one.

q.t: What is the largest 2-digit even number?
q.e: The largest 2-digit number is 99, which is odd, so step back one to 98.

q.t: 35 coins are put into pairs. How many full pairs are made?
q.e: 17 pairs use 34 coins; 1 coin is left over because 35 is odd.

q.t: Using only ₹10, ₹5, ₹2 and ₹1 coins, what is the fewest number of coins that make ₹36?
q.e: Use the biggest coins first: three ₹10 (₹30), one ₹5 (₹35), one ₹1 (₹36) — 5 coins.

q.t: Gundappa has 6 rows of 8 coconut trees. He plucks 5 coconuts from each tree. How many coconuts does he pluck?
q.e: There are 6 × 8 = 48 trees, and 48 groups of 5 coconuts make 240.

q.t: 4 trays are stacked. Each tray has 3 rows of 4 laddoos and 2 rows of 4 pedas. How many sweets in all?
q.e: One tray has 12 laddoos + 8 pedas = 20 sweets, and 4 trays have 80.

q.t: Using two different digits from 3, 4 and 7, how many even 2-digit numbers can you make?
q.k: len([a*10+b for a in (3,4,7) for b in (3,4,7) if a!=b and b%2==0])
q.e: An even number must end in 4, so the numbers are 34 and 74.

q.t: Using the digits 2, 5 and 8 once each, how many 3-digit odd numbers can you make?
q.e: An odd number must end in 5; the other two digits can go 2-8 or 8-2: 285 and 825.

q.t: Add all the numbers from 1 to 10. Is the total even or odd?
q.e: The even numbers pair up fully; the five odd numbers each have one left over, and five left-overs make two pairs plus one alone — so the total (55) is odd.

q.t: Take any odd number, add 1 to it, and then double the answer. The result is:
q.e: Doubling makes two equal groups, so every item has a partner — any doubled number is even.

q.t: Shirley’s book has pages numbered 1 to 48. How many pages have odd numbers?
q.k: len([x for x in range(1,49) if x%2])
q.e: Odd and even pages take turns, so half of 48 pages are odd: 24.

q.t: Shiv has 47 coins and Shirley has 52 coins. They put all their coins together into pairs. How many full pairs do they make?
q.e: Together they have 99 coins; 49 pairs use 98 and 1 is left over.

q.t: Ramesh has 3 stacks of 10 coins of ₹5 and 4 more coins of ₹2. How much money does he have (in ₹)?
q.e: 30 coins of ₹5 make ₹150, and 4 coins of ₹2 add ₹8.

q.t: Make ₹125 using only ₹10 and ₹5 coins, with as many ₹10 coins as possible. How many coins do you use in all?
q.e: 12 coins of ₹10 make ₹120; one ₹5 coin makes the last ₹5 — 13 coins.
